Optimization guidance: Target: Apple M3 Pro, 14 GPU cores. Optimize synchronized public-call latency against the fastest verified PyTorch baseline. Inductor and functional RMSNorm can beat eager PyTorch. This experiment assumes callers guarantee the value domain. Use the runtime SIMD width when needed. Think about memory passes, synchronization and work per thread. Pick one concrete hypothesis. If feedback shows a compile or correctness failure, fix it first. If feedback shows a correct but slow kernel, target the strongest baseline and change one major aspect of the schedule.
Operation guidance: Fuse the bias add and GELU into one pass. For narrow or odd rows, compare flat scalar threads with several adjacent columns per thread. Use vector loads only when every row address is aligned and handle all tail elements. Minimize indexing and repeated loads.
Use consistent scalar or vector grid coordinate types. Use parentheses around a vector pointer cast before indexing. For shared reductions in multiple phases use distinct scratch or a uniform barrier after all reads before reuse.
